- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.20) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.30) and prices are rising, model often overshoots; cap upward revisions after spikes.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — apply downward bias to first 5–7 days.
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., sharp drop after peak), model often fails to correct — adjust forecast to align with recent 7–14 day average.
- If sentiment history shows strong positive momentum followed by a drop, model tends to lag — forecast should be slightly ahead of true outcome in the first 3–5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if model shows consistent upward trend with no recent reversal, reduce final 5–7 days to avoid overconfidence bias.
- If sentiment is volatile or mixed, model often averages out extremes — use sentiment-weighted smoothing to avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment shifts.
